_description: Cross-cutting architectural decisions (layer structure, contracts). Module-specific decisions live in their own decisions.jsonl.

decision: Three-layer split: app (client), server, shared (types only)
reasoning: Security: AI keys never leave the server. Testability: server logic is pure Node with no DOM dependency. Clarity: each layer has one responsibility and a clear import direction.
alternatives: Nuxt 3 pattern with no explicit shared layer
outcome: Layer boundaries are enforced at the import level; Nuxt 4 auto-imports shared types on both sides

decision: Shared types via Nuxt 4 auto-imports from shared/types/
reasoning: Single source of truth for the client–server API contract. No manual import statements. Shape errors are caught at compile time on both sides simultaneously.
alternatives: Separate npm package for shared types
outcome: Types are always in sync; no import boilerplate

decision: Game data as TS consts in server/data/ (never sent raw to client)
reasoning: Copyright: rulebook text stays server-private. Type safety: shape errors caught at compile time. No DB needed for initial versions.
outcome: Data is typed, server-private, and zero-dependency; DB migration would only touch server/services/rpg/
